question.problem:
Evaluate the mixed integral

$$
{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}5yz\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A
$$

given that the region $D$ in the $xz$-plane is given by

$$
D=\{(x,z)\,:\,0\le z\le 2,\,0\le x\le 2-z\}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we evaluate the inner integral with respect to $y,$ treating $z$ and $x$ as constants:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}[{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}5yz\,\text{d}y]\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}5z{[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{∬}_{D}z(4-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $D$ is a type II region in the $xz$-plane.
Therefore, to evaluate our double integral as a repeated integral over this region, we integrate with respect to $x$ and then with respect to $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{2}{∬}_{D}z(4-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}A & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{2-z}z(4-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}z[{\int }_{0}^{2-z}(4-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x]\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}z{[(4x-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})]}_{x=0}^{x=2-z}\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}z(4(2-z)-\frac{(2-z)^{3}}{3})\,\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(\frac{16z}{3}-2{z}^{3}+\frac{{z}^{4}}{3})\,\text{d}z \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{[\frac{8{z}^{2}}{3}-\frac{{z}^{4}}{2}+\frac{{z}^{5}}{15}]}_{z=0}^{z=2} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}[\frac{32}{3}-8+\frac{32}{15}] \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$
